subject: microbiology
title: Orientia tsutsugamushi, Eschar and Weil-Felix Testing

steps.tx: **Orientia tsutsugamushi** differs from Rickettsia by lacking classic lipopolysaccharide and peptidoglycan architecture, yet it likewise lives intracellularly and injures endothelium. It has multiple antigenic strains, limiting cross protection. Humans acquire it through chigger bites while working or travelling through scrub vegetation. Rodents are important hosts for mites, but the mite itself can maintain the organism transovarially.
steps.say: Orientia is the mite borne endothelial pathogen behind scrub typhus.

vis.alt: Rickettsial disease clues with eschars and vector associated rash
vis.caption: Eschar and rash patterns help separate scrub typhus from other febrile illnesses.

steps.tx: An **eschar** begins as a papule at the chigger bite, ulcerates and forms a dark crust with an erythematous halo. It may be hidden in the groin, axilla, inframammary fold, waistline or genital area, so a complete skin examination matters in undifferentiated fever. The eschar is both a diagnostic clue and the highest-yield specimen site for PCR before antibiotics sterilise the lesion.
steps.say: Search hidden folds for an eschar; absence after a quick glance does not exclude scrub typhus.

right.title: Sample value
points: Eschar swab or crust for PCR
Can remain positive after blood PCR falls

steps.tx: The **Weil Felix test** detects cross reactive antibodies that agglutinate certain Proteus strains. OXK reactivity is associated with scrub typhus, OX19 with typhus group rickettsiae, and OX2 mainly with spotted fever group patterns. It is inexpensive but has poor sensitivity and specificity, cross reacts with Proteus urinary infection and other conditions, and should not be treated as a rule out test.
steps.say: Weil Felix patterns are historical clues, not precise proof of a rickettsial species.

left.title: Classical patterns
points: OX19 predominant in epidemic and murine typhus
Patterns overlap and vary by timing

right.title: Limitations
points: Single titre interpretation depends on local background
Modern IgM ELISA, IFA and PCR perform better

steps.tx: Scrub typhus can progress to **pneumonitis, meningoencephalitis, hepatitis, acute kidney injury, myocarditis and multiorgan dysfunction**. Thrombocytopenia and transaminitis support systemic endothelial disease but are not specific. Severe presentations need organ support plus a rickettsial active antibiotic. Geographic overlap with leptospirosis, dengue, malaria and typhoid means empirical doxycycline decisions often occur within a broader tropical fever protocol.
steps.say: Scrub typhus can be multiorgan disease, not merely a fever with an eschar.

right.title: Clinical overlap
points: Leptospirosis adds jaundice and renal injury
Malaria requires smear or antigen exclusion
Typhoid has sustained fever and abdominal features

steps.tx: **Doxycycline responsiveness** is supportive but not diagnostic proof because many tropical infections fluctuate and doxycycline also treats leptospirosis and some other bacterial diseases. Azithromycin is an option in pregnancy and in regions or studies with doxycycline reduced response. Rifampicin has been used in selected areas. Persistent fever after forty eight to seventy two hours should trigger a search for complications or a different diagnosis.
steps.say: Improvement on doxycycline supports the plan but never proves scrub typhus alone.

left.title: Therapy options
points: Severe disease may require ICU support
Treat promptly without waiting for paired serology

right.title: Reassess when
points: Laboratory evidence points to another cause
Abscess, malaria or bacterial sepsis is suspected

steps.tx: Prevention focuses on **avoiding chigger bites** and reducing exposure in mite habitats: protective clothing, repellents, clearing vegetation around camps where feasible, and not sitting or sleeping directly on grass in endemic areas. There is no licensed vaccine. Rodent control without mite control can worsen or fail to interrupt transmission because trombiculid mites maintain Orientia across generations.
steps.say: For scrub typhus prevention, the mite is the target, not rodents alone.
